title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page, following Katz-Oda): X --f--> S --g--> T with f smooth. Then 0 -> f^*Omega^1_{S/T} -> Omega^1_{X/T} -> Omega^1_{X/S} -> 0 is exact. Its exterior powers give the Koszul filtration Fil^p_{X/S} of the relative de Rham complex Omega^._{X/T}. Its graded pieces are Gr^p = f^*Omega^p_{S/T} (x) Omega^._{X/S}[-p] (formula (2)). Flatness lets one write these as derived tensors (formula (2')). Applying Rf_* gives a filtered object of a filtered derived category.

On this page:
(i) Gr^p commutes with Rf_*.
(ii) For f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the projection formula gives (3): Gr^p Rf_*(Omega_{X/T}) = Omega^p_{S/T} (x)^L Rf_*(Omega^._{X/S})[-p]. Grothendieck flags this as 'dans un cadre pas très catholique'. The reason is that the differential of Omega^._{X/S} is f^{-1}O_S-linear but not O_X-linear, so the usual projection formula for quasi-coherent modules needs checking.
(iii) The filtration gives connecting morphisms d_1^{(p)}: Gr^p -> Gr^{p+1}[1] (formula (4)). Rewritten via (3) and shifted by p, these are maps Omega^p_{S/T} (x)^L Rf_*Omega_{X/S} -> Omega^{p+1}_{S/T} (x)^L Rf_*Omega_{X/S} (formulas (5), (6)).
(iv) d_1^{(p+1)} d_1^{(p)} = 0 (formula (7)). The composite of two consecutive connecting maps of a filtered object vanishes, since it factors through the triangle for Fil^p/Fil^{p+2}.
(v) For p = 0 one gets nabla: Rf_*(Omega_{X/S}) -> Omega^1_{S/T} (x) Rf_*(Omega_{X/S}). This is the Gauss-Manin connection, defined at the level of the derived pushforward rather than on its cohomology sheaves. (7) is invoked for integrability.
(vi) Grothendieck remarks that this seems to coincide with the connection he defined elsewhere, presumably the crystalline definition in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1966/68); the reference is left blank.
(vii) A marginal warning says one must prove a compatibility of d_1 with the differential of Omega_{S/T} (a Leibniz rule) before (7) can be read as integrability.

The next page passes to cohomology sheaves, (8)/(8'), when S is formally smooth over T. It then builds the Katz-Oda spectral sequence for RGamma(S, K) = RH_DR(X/T). This is the standard Katz-Oda construction (1968), with Grothendieck attempting to lift it to the derived category.
errors: The derived-level statement is incomplete, as the marginal note itself admits. d_1^{(0)} is only a morphism of complexes of g^{-1}O_T-modules in the derived category; it is not O_S-linear. Calling it a 'connection' on the object Rf_*(Omega_{X/S}) requires a Leibniz compatibility relating d_1^{(0)}, d_1^{(1)} and d_{S/T}, which is not proved here.
d_1^{(1)} on Omega^1 (x) Rf_*(Omega_{X/S}) must be identified with the canonical extension of nabla before (7) gives integrability nabla^2 = 0. This identification is also unproved.

Even granted that, d^2 = 0 holding only as an equation of morphisms in the derived category does not give a coherent derived integrable connection; that would need higher homotopies. Strictly, only the cohomology-level statement (8') on the next page is fully justified, and that is how Katz-Oda work.
Minor: (6') writes a plain tensor instead of a derived tensor. This is harmless when Omega^1_{S/T} is flat, but inconsistent with (5)/(6).

ideas.what: Koszul filtration of Omega_{X/T} by powers of f^*Omega^1_{S/T}, with graded pieces f^*Omega^p_{S/T} (x) Omega_{X/S}[-p]
ideas.where_published: Katz-Oda, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 1968; Katz, Publ. IHES 39

ideas.what: Gauss-Manin connection as the d_1 connecting map of the filtered object Rf_*(Omega_{X/T}), with integrability from d_1^2 = 0
ideas.modern_name: Gauss-Manin connection via the Katz-Oda spectral sequence
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), crystalline construction

ideas.what: Attempt to define the connection on the derived pushforward Rf_*(Omega_{X/S}) itself, via a projection formula for non-O-linear complexes in a filtered derived category
ideas.modern_name: Derived/dg Gauss-Manin connection; D-module or crystal structure on the derived pushforward
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later dg and infinity-categorical treatments (various authors); filtered derived categories from Illusie

missed.claim: Grothendieck notices that a derived-category-level Gauss-Manin connection needs a separately proved Leibniz compatibility with d_{S/T}, and that the projection formula for complexes with differential-operator differentials is 'pas très catholique'. He leaves both unchecked and drops to cohomology sheaves on the next page. This anticipates the need for an enhanced, dg or infinity-categorical, framework for connections on derived pushforwards. That framework was later developed by others, so this is a historical anticipation rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: Attention, il faut prouver une compatibilité de d_1 avec diff. de Omega_{S/T} !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it shows awareness of the limits of triangulated categories for such structures. The mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mostly a faithful reworking of Katz-Oda, with a mild attempt to work at the derived level and an honest note about a gap. The remark identifying it with his own crystalline Gauss-Manin connection is well known in substance. Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Margin note reads roughly: 'Attention, il faut prouver une compatibilité de d_1 avec diff. de Omega_{S/T} ! ... pour expliciter comme il est dit (7) !' The bracketed part is illegible; the '[?]' in the transcription is uncertain.
Line 4: 'il résulte {+alors+} de la formule de projection': the inserted word above the line appears to be 'alors'.
After 'On a', the struck-through phrase is uncertain (transcribed as 'en particulier en opérateurs'); what remains is 'On a une différentielle'.
In (6) the label is written 'd_1^{(p)}[p]', with a struck mark before it.
